identification.summary: WASSONITE is the Dragos name for an ICS/OT-focused activity group (third-party catalogs describe it as North Korea-linked [S8]); Dragos first identified it after a malware intrusion at the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant (KKNPP) in India [S1]. Activity dates to at least 2018 [S1].
identification.notes: Dragos (not Microsoft or MITRE) is the naming vendor; no Microsoft name or MITRE group ID was found. Dragos describes some similarity to its COVELLITE group (also tied to Lazarus) but says COVELLITE uses different capabilities and targets [S1]. AppleSeed is also reported by Malwarebytes in Kimsuky activity against South Korean government targets [S7]; none of the sources reviewed establish whether WASSONITE and Kimsuky are the same cluster, so they are not merged here.

attribution.sponsor: North Korea (per third-party catalog Malpedia and indirect Lazarus/DTrack links; Dragos pages reviewed do not state it directly)
attribution.confidence: Not stated numerically in the sources reviewed; the North Korea link is a vendor assessment, not a government attribution.
attribution.basis: Malpedia describes WASSONITE as a North Korea-linked APT [S8]. The link is indirect: security firms associate DTrack with Lazarus [S4], and Dragos pages reviewed do not state a North Korea attribution directly [S1]. Kaspersky tied DTrack to Lazarus through code overlap with the 2013 DarkSeoul campaign, including a shared C2 protocol implementation [S4]. NPCIL did not attribute the Kudankulam infection; the Lazarus link there rests on researcher analysis [S5].

objectives: Dragos reports activity limited to IT-network access at Stage 1 of the ICS kill chain, with no ICS-specific disruptive or destructive capability observed [S1]. The stated objective is not given in the sources; the pattern of access, reconnaissance and data collection against industrial and nuclear-sector targets is consistent with espionage, but this is not stated by a cited source.

targeting.notes: Dragos reports targeting of Asian entities, largely in India, and possibly Japan and South Korea [S1]. The Kudankulam plant infection was on an internet-connected administrative network that NPCIL said was isolated from the critical internal network [S5].

capabilities.summary: Dragos reports WASSONITE uses DTrack for remote access, Mimikatz for credential theft, and built-in system utilities for lateral movement and file transfer, and has used nuclear-themed phishing lures to deliver the AppleSeed backdoor [S1]. Kaspersky describes DTrack as a RAT with keylogging, browser history retrieval, process and network enumeration and file listing, delivered via multiple droppers and using process hollowing [S3][S4].

campaigns.name: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant intrusion (DTrack)
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky publicly described DTrack on 2019-09-23, with last observed activity in early September 2019 [S2][S3]. NPCIL later confirmed malware on an administrative-network computer at Kudankulam, saying CERT-In had flagged it on 4 September 2019 [S5]. Dragos says it identified WASSONITE following this intrusion [S1]. The Lazarus link here rests on researcher analysis, not an official attribution [S5].

campaigns.name: AppleSeed backdoor activity against industrial victims
campaigns.summary: Dragos reports WASSONITE used nuclear energy-themed spear-phishing lures to deliver the AppleSeed backdoor [S1]. Dragos said it monitored and reported renewed WASSONITE activity in 2021 [S6]. Details of victim counts are not confirmed in an opened source (see gaps).

diamond.adversary: Activity group tracked by Dragos as WASSONITE, described by third parties as North Korea-linked with indirect Lazarus connections [S1][S8].
diamond.capability: DTrack RAT, Mimikatz, AppleSeed backdoor, native system utilities [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: AppleSeed command-and-control servers are referenced by Dragos, but specifics were not obtained from an opened source.
diamond.victim: Nuclear energy, electric generation, manufacturing and space-research organizations, mainly India [S1].
diamond.technology: Windows IT networks, including internet-connected administrative networks at industrial sites [S1][S5].

gaps: The Dragos WASSONITE profile and Dragos reports could not be opened (fetch tool failed with DNS errors); Dragos claims rely on search-result summaries of the profile, and the profile page is undated.

Dragos reporting of June 2021 victims in oil and gas, electric and component manufacturing communicating with a WASSONITE AppleSeed C2 (seen only in a search summary of an Automation.com article, not opened or dated) is unverified here.
Whether WASSONITE overlaps with Kimsuky (AppleSeed) or Lazarus sub-clusters is unresolved.
No Microsoft name, MITRE group ID, or government attribution found.
Victim counts, C2 infrastructure, intrusion dates after 2021 and any ICS-impacting activity are unknown.
Primary Kaspersky technical blog and NPCIL statement were not opened; coverage was used.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: relevant environment is IT and administrative networks of nuclear, electric, manufacturing and space-research entities in India and possibly Japan and South Korea [S1][S5]. Step 3: the adversary has shown Stage 1 ICS kill chain access only, no disruptive capability [S1]. MLCOA: continued spear-phishing (nuclear-themed lures) delivering AppleSeed/DTrack, credential theft with Mimikatz and lateral movement to collect data [S1]. MDCOA: pivot from IT to OT; no cited source shows this capability. Candidate indicators: nuclear-themed phishing lures, DTrack and AppleSeed artifacts, Mimikatz use, outbound traffic from administrative networks to known C2 [S1][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track vendor reporting on DTrack and AppleSeed and share indicators with allied energy-sector partners; the Kudankulam case showed an operator may initially deny an intrusion, so cross-check [S5]. Authorities and coordination: reporting relies on commercial intelligence and foreign operator statements; sharing with partners requires proper release channels. Mission assurance: segment administrative networks from control networks, as NPCIL claimed for Kudankulam, and verify the claim [S5].
